title: Compiler diagnostics are structured only at the external CLI boundary
observed_need: Compile-fail and diagnostic tests must match diagnostic identity and preserve source spans without scraping human prose.
current_language_behavior: The Rust toolchain exposes versioned structured diagnostics and the native runner fail-closes on invalid admission. P-062 added a Test-owned MNCS application that projects diagnostic codes and applies compile verdict policy without building a host diagnostic-code list. P-063 replaces the verdict application's Test JsonValue tree projection with bounded Stdlib JSON cursor events and a syntax validator. P-064 added bounded native typed records for standard diagnostic objects; P-065 extended them with expected tokens and one level of related diagnostics. P-066 replaced the diagnostic projector's JsonValue tree traversal with a second bounded json_cursor pass over the original chunked bytes. P-067 retires the fixed native diagnostic-record output array and Python reconstruction mapper: MNCS validates the selected array and returns its source span, then Python decodes only that span for the public dictionary contract. P-068 removes the redundant per-field typed validation buffers; the native cursor now validates JSON and selection metadata, bounds the selected array, and preserves arbitrary diagnostic JSON values in the selected span. P-069 initially fed the selected span through the Test-owned MNCS JSON token tape, where Python assembled public lists and dictionaries from native structural events. P-070 replaces that compile-entry projection with bounded typed diagnostic-code values plus the selected diagnostic-array source span from the native verdict application. Python decodes only code bytes for compile policy and carries the diagnostic array opaquely into the native public-result key-order and window formatter; it does not build diagnostic lists or dictionaries on the ordinary supported path. The formatter emits 4,096-byte windows and carries source SHA-256 state across continuations, checking the full input digest on the final window rather than rehashing it on every call. The 29,188-byte nested differential case completed in ten native calls with its 37,377-byte output and digest matching the independent golden under the existing step ceiling. The native_compile_diagnostic_records helper materializes records only for Python API-boundary callers. MNCS application code still cannot directly consume compiler Diagnostic values.
why_insufficient: The Test adapter still decodes bounded typed diagnostic-code bytes for policy fields, and final results cross the structured CLI JSON boundary. The native diagnostic application admits documents up to 16,384 bytes and up to 32 selected object records; unsupported shapes, excessive nesting, over-bound values, native budget exhaustion, and oversized documents retain the atomic Python JSON compatibility path. The explicit native_compile_diagnostic_records Python API wrapper still materializes a selected array when a caller requests dictionaries.
minimal_reproducer: tests/fixtures/compile_fail.mncs plus tools/mncs_test.py: compile_entry sends compiler output to the native diagnostic verdict and span applications, carries the selected array bytes opaquely into the Test public-result serializer, and uses native typed code values for failure policy.
desired_direction: A versioned diagnostic value/protocol exposing code, severity, source span, related diagnostics, and rendered forms to native tooling.
workaround: The Test-owned MNCS diagnostic application validates the bounded compiler document, applies compile-verdict policy, returns typed code values and the selected root, errors, or diagnostics array span when it has at most 32 object records, and preserves the span as opaque bytes through the normal result envelope. The native public-result key-order and window formatter preserve canonical sorted JSON and digest output without Python diagnostic containers. The public API wrapper may materialize records on explicit request; unsupported or over-bound documents use the full Python compatibility parser atomically. No formatted-stderr parsing is used.
